newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurers to end London joint venture.
newsitem.headline: German insurers to end London joint venture.

text.p: German insurers Wuerttembergische Versicherung AG and Gerling-Konzern Allgemeine Versicherung AG will in future go their separate ways in London, the companies said on Monday.
Wuerttembergische will on January 1, 1998 take over Gerling's stake in WG Underwriting Services (WGUS), John Solder, managing director of WGUS, said.

The joint venture was set up in 1992 to represent both companies' marine and aviation underwriting interests in London. In 1996, premium income reached 22.5 million stg, of which 12.5 million was marine and 10 million aviation, Solder said.
Wuerttembergische is expected to pay only a nominal sum for the stake, but a final decision on that has not been taken yet, the company said in Stuttgart.

Gerling London Managing Director Bjorn Jansli said that Gerling was withdrawing in order to develop further its international strategy. It was the company's aim to become a leader in marine and aviation business worldwide.
Gerling is one of Germany's major insurers, with 1996 group premium income of 11.0 billion marks. Wuerttembergische recorded 4.8 billion marks.
Solder said the "friendly relationship" between the companies would continue. WGUS will manage the run-off of the Gerling business it had handled so far, he said.
Wuerttembergische said in Stuttgart that it will retain its presence in London.
Jurgen Hoffmann, board member of Wuerttembergische and chairman of WGUS, said the German insurer will continue to develop aviation, hull, cargo and specie business in London.

Wuerttembergische was pleased with the performance of WGUS and was seeking "an increased involvement and profile in the London market." Wuerttembergische expects to keep WGUS' volume at the present level, despite Gerling's withdrawal.
